rv.q: Ultimately, theatergoers will be moved by the dramatic finale, and probably be familiar with some of the score.
The coffee-shop conceit is brilliant and the production, directed by Matthew Silar, is a wonder.
Godspell is just a story of a man, told through the eyes of another man, and performed by exceptionally talented individuals.
The 2.25 hours, including intermission, were so worth it.
But though it's not the most emotionally layered way of explicating the entwined costs and joys of embracing communality over individuality, the show still has its endearing moments.
The cast features a fabulous array of spirited performing artists who do a great job revving up the audience with their loud and charismatic approach to the Gospel.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive revival of "Godspell" for its modern coffeehouse setting and contemporary relevance. The production successfully updates Schwartz's classic musical for today's audiences with engaging performances and fresh staging.
